newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen shares end higher on credit-easing hopes.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen shares end higher on credit-easing hopes.

text.p: Shenzhen's A and B share indices fluctuated in a narrow band for most of Friday's session before closing higher on market talk that China plans to further ease its credit controls soon, brokers said.
The B share index edged up 1.27 points or 0.90 percent to close at 142.00 on volume of 9.57 million shares worth HK$47.68 million compared with Thursday's HK$67.41 million.
The A share index rose 3.62 points or 1.08 percent to end at 337.24 on turnover of 3.71 billion yuan against 2.94 billion yuan in the previous session.

The talk of a possible easing of credit controls through a reduction in bank reserve requirements fueled speculative buying in financial counters and boosted the A share index, with the B share market moving up in tandem, brokers said.
Despite the rises, institutions largely adopted a wait-and-see attitude towards trading ahead of the weekend, a broker at China Guotai Securities Co Ltd said.
"It remains unclear as to whether the upward trend can extend into next week," a trader said.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen was the biggest B share gainer, rising HK$0.11 or 3.03 percent to HK$3.74 on volume of 165,900 shares on speculative buying.
China Bicycle edged up HK$0.08 to HK$3.19 on trade of 269,900 shares, the second sharpest gainer.

Changan Automobile was most active on volume of 1.39 million shares and added HK$0.03 to HK$4.51. Hotelier Dadonghai put on HK$0.05 to HK$3.65 on the session's second heaviest trade of 966,000 shares.
Selling was focused on cheap-priced issues, with Tellus Machinery losing HK$0.04 to HK$2.81, brokers said.
Wholesaler Shenzhen Agricultural Products Co Ltd, which listed 19 million A shares in Shenzhen on Friday, ended the session at 21.14 yuan against an offer price of 8.38 yuan per share last month.

Kunming Department Store, which owns a share of in a private bank, closed at its 10 percent limit-up of 6.99 yuan on heavy volume of 11.07 million shares on speculative demand from institutions, brokers said.
Xinjiang Hongyuan Trust followed suit, ending at 10.55 yuan with 9.9 million shares changing hands.
